info.description:
AI-Ready API Gateway & MCP Orchestrator. Decomposes a carrier's monolithic, proprietary Policy Administration APIs into atomic OpenAPI 3.1 operations, translates them live to each vendor's dialect, exposes them over the Model Context Protocol for AI agents, and orchestrates them into business workflows with retries and compensation.

**Problem.** Legacy PAS APIs are monolithic, use proprietary DSLs and are not discoverable by AI agents. An agent cannot call an operation it cannot discover, describe or authorise separately - which is why 90% of carriers' AI pilots stall at the integration layer rather than at the model.

Every atomic operation is exposed three ways with one definition: as a REST endpoint (`/insurance/v1/...`), as an MCP tool over streamable HTTP at `/mcp`, and as a catalogued entry at `/operations`. The OpenAPI document is generated from the same declarations, so the spec cannot drift from behaviour.
info.title: plugin1 - PAS Plugins

post.description: Submits an application into the carrier's underwriting queue. Plugin 3's workbench calls this after triage; direct API clients call it when they want the carrier's own underwriter rather than an automated decision.
post.x-pas-intent: Start underwriting on a new application

get.description: Retrieve an application
get.x-pas-intent: Check the underwriting status and outstanding requirements

post.description: Issues a policy. Requires an accepted quote; the workflow in plugin 1 validates eligibility, underwriting status and funding before calling this operation. Always send an Idempotency-Key: a retried bind against a live PAS would otherwise create a second policy.

200.description: Bind a policy from a quote

post.summary: Bind a policy from a quote
post.x-pas-intent: Convert an accepted quote into an issued, in-force policy

post.description: Pure rating computation. Nothing is written to the carrier's records, so it is safe for an agent to call speculatively while exploring options. Returns the rating-factor breakdown so an underwriter can challenge individual components.
post.x-pas-intent: Price a hypothetical policy without creating anything

post.description: Paginated search across the caller's tenant. Filters are explicit and combinable; omitted filters match everything.
post.x-pas-intent: List policies matching a filter, for reconciliation and reporting

get.description: Returns the full canonical policy record. This is the single read that an agent should use to understand a policy; it never mutates anything and is safe to call repeatedly.
get.x-pas-intent: Read the current state of one policy by policy number

get.description: List beneficiaries
get.x-pas-intent: See the current beneficiary schedule and signature state

put.description: Replaces the whole beneficiary schedule (PUT semantics - not a delta). Shares may total less than 100 percent, in which case the remainder stays with the existing default beneficiary; they may never exceed 100 percent. With requireAllSignatures the change is staged pending counter-signature and is committed to the plugin 7 ledger once every party has signed.
put.x-pas-intent: Change who receives the death benefit

post.description: Returns the three figures a surrender conversation needs, and can project them forward. netCashValue is cashValue less any outstanding policy loan.
post.x-pas-intent: Read cash, surrender and net cash values for a policy

get.description: Ordered lifecycle events: issue, changes, premium status changes, lapse, reinstatement, surrender. Correlates with the plugin 7 ledger history.
get.x-pas-intent: See every lifecycle event recorded against a policy

post.description: Moves the policy to 'lapsed'. The request must carry confirmation=true: policy-state changes are irreversible in most cores, and an agent must state its intent explicitly rather than firing a mutation by side effect.
post.x-pas-intent: Move an in-force policy to lapsed status

post.description: Advances cash against the policy's surrender value. The PAS enforces the maximum loan percentage and the free-look restriction on new policies.
post.x-pas-intent: Borrow against a policy's cash value

post.description: Moves the policy to 'active'. The request must carry confirmation=true: policy-state changes are irreversible in most cores, and an agent must state its intent explicitly rather than firing a mutation by side effect.
post.x-pas-intent: Return a lapsed policy to active status

get.description: A cheap status probe. Use this instead of `policy.get` when the status is the only thing needed - it is materially faster on a loaded PAS.
get.x-pas-intent: Check only the current status of a policy

post.description: Moves the policy to 'surrendered'. The request must carry confirmation=true: policy-state changes are irreversible in most cores, and an agent must state its intent explicitly rather than firing a mutation by side effect.
post.x-pas-intent: Surrender an in-force policy for its cash surrender value

post.description: Moves the policy to 'terminated'. The request must carry confirmation=true: policy-state changes are irreversible in most cores, and an agent must state its intent explicitly rather than firing a mutation by side effect.
post.x-pas-intent: Terminate a policy without a cash payout, e.g. on underwriting grounds

get.description: List available products
get.x-pas-intent: Discover which products a carrier will currently sell

get.description: Issue ages, face-amount bounds, riders and filed states. This is what an agent should read before quoting a product it has not seen before.
get.x-pas-intent: Read what a product is and what it allows

get.description: List recent quotes
get.x-pas-intent: Find quotes created recently, for conversion reporting

post.description: Creates a bindable quote with a validity window. Re-sending the same Idempotency-Key returns the original quote rather than creating a duplicate. An accepted quote is the only legal input to `policy.bind`.
post.x-pas-intent: Persist a price that can later be converted into a policy

get.description: Retrieve a quote
get.x-pas-intent: Read back a previously created quote
